newsitem.title: USA: US Treasuries end down, jitters ahead of Greenspan.
newsitem.headline: US Treasuries end down, jitters ahead of Greenspan.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries ended weaker on Friday as positions were lightened ahead of Federal Reserve chairman's Humphrey Hawkins testimony next week.
The 30-year bond closed at 101-10/32, down 14/32 from Thursday. Its yield rose to 6.52 percent from 6.49 percent.
"Guys just wanted to lighten up," said a senior trader at a promary dealership. "There are more bearish bets going into Humphrey Hawkins than bullish."
Greenspan will give his testimony on the state of the economy to Congress beginning on Tuesday morning.
"I don't think the market is leaning in either direction (in anticipating Greenspan's comments,)" said the trader. "But the risk is more to the downside than upside."
Traders noted that the market has had a good run higher, but there is very little room to rally further -- unless the Fed does the unlikely and cuts rates.

"With the market where it is, Greenspan will probably take a more cautious tone than bullish tone," said Scott Graham, co-head trader at Prudential Securities Inc. "He doesn't want the market to get much higher."
Jitters over Greenspan's testimony only added to the negative tone seen from the start of trading.
Treasury prices opened lower after profit-taking during the Tokyo and London sessions during the night, only to move off early lows on a weaker-than-expected U.S. trade report.
The Commerce Department said the U.S. trade gap widened 17 percent in May to $10.23 billion from an $8.75 billion deficit in April.
But Treasuries fell again after the University of Michigan reported that its preliminary July consumer sentiment index rose to 106.4 from June's 104.5 reading.
Market participants said the selling was mainly by retail accounts -- primarily non-U.S.
The rest of the day featured solid two-way flows, including central bank buying, hedge fund buying and selling and one big sale of 10-year notes.
Traders noted that the 10-year sector was hit hardest this session, with the 10-year note down 10/32 to 102-26/32, yielding 6.24 percent.
Yet, activity was very thin. Volume was only about $50 billion, according to GovPX. Volume is seen staying thin and dealers predicted tight ranges to persist until Tuesday.
In late trading, the two-year note was down 2/32 at 100-6/32 to yield 5.89 percent, the five-year note fell 6/32 to 100-14/32 to yield 6.15 percent.
The bill sector was also hit hard.

The three-month bill was up three basis points at a discount rate of 5.11 percent, the six-month was up four basis points at 5.15 percent and the one-year bill was up six basis points at 5.28 percent.
